(Capacity: 19,368) |champion= |tourney= [[2023 NCAA Division I men's basketball tournament|NCAA tournament]] |tourney_result= Sweet Sixteen }} {{2022–23 Southeastern Conference men's basketball standings}} The '''2022–23 Arkansas Razorbacks men's basketball team''' represented the [[University of Arkansas]] during the [[2022–23 NCAA Division I men's basketball season]]. The team was led by fourth-year head coach [[Eric Musselman]], and played its home games at [[Bud Walton Arena]] in [[Fayetteville, Arkansas]] as a member of the [[Southeastern Conference]]. They finished the season 19–12, 8–10 in SEC Play to finish in a tie for 9th place. In the [[2023 SEC men's basketball tournament|SEC tournament]], the Razorbacks defeated [[2022–23 Auburn Tigers men's basketball team|Auburn]] in the second round before being defeated by [[2022–23 Texas A&M Aggies men's basketball team|Texas A&M]] in the quarterfinals. They received an at-large bid to the [[2023 NCAA Division I men's basketball tournament|NCAA Tournament]] as a No. 8 seed in the West Region. They defeated [[2022–23 Illinois Fighting Illini men's basketball team|Illinois]] in the first round and upset No. 1 seed [[2022–23 Kansas Jayhawks men's basketball team|Kansas]] to reach the Sweet Sixteen. There, they were defeated by No. 4 seed, and eventual tournament champions, [[2022–23 UConn Huskies men's basketball team|UConn]], ending their season with an overall 22–14 record. ==Previous season== {{main|2021–22 Arkansas Razorbacks men's basketball team}} Arkansas followed up an Elite Eight appearance in 2021 with another in 2022, even though the Razorbacks didn't finish as high in the SEC as they had a year prior. This time they were fourth in the final SEC standings, and earned a 4 seed in the [[2022 NCAA Division I men's basketball tournament|NCAA tournament]]. Arkansas was sent to Buffalo, New York where they dispatched Vermont and New Mexico State to advance to the Sweet 16 for the second year in a row.{{cite web | url=https://arkansasrazorbacks.com/sweet-16-hogs-hold-off-nmsu-to-advance-to-second-straight-sweet-16/ | title=SWEET 16! Hogs hold off NMSU to advance to second straight Sweet 16 | date=19 March 2022 | access-date=30 June 2022 | archive-date=2 June 2022 | archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20220602032232/https://arkansasrazorbacks.com/sweet-16-hogs-hold-off-nmsu-to-advance-to-second-straight-sweet-16/ | url-status=live }} In the regional semifinals against overall top seeded Gonzaga, Arkansas secured a 74–68 upset victory at the [[Chase Center]] in San Francisco.{{cite web | url=https://www.si.com/college/2022/03/25/arkansas-upsets-no-1-gonzaga-in-sweet-16-advances-to-elite-eight | title=No. 4 Arkansas Shocks No. 1 Overall Seed Gonzaga in Sweet 16 | access-date=2022-06-30 | archive-date=2022-06-30 | archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20220630055816/https://www.si.com/college/2022/03/25/arkansas-upsets-no-1-gonzaga-in-sweet-16-advances-to-elite-eight | url-status=live }} This set up an Elite Eight showdown with Duke, in the final year of head coach [[Mike Krzyzewski]]'s 43-year stint with the Blue Devils. Duke defeated the Razorbacks 78–69 to advance to the Final Four.
